title: Introduce observability-orbit priority-sparkline and adaptive-alert-dampener
author: Maya Gonzalez
description: Motivation: Long-running incidents caused by noisy token-level spikes and high-cardinality tenant metrics have forced oncall to manually tune alerts per-customer. This PR introduces three coordinated observability features to reduce alert churn and improve operator signal-to-noise: 1) observability-orbit: a compact invocation-level provenance metric that maps token-phase timing across service boundaries (prefix, model, postprocess) to a single orbit id. 2) priority-sparkline: an inline, per-tenant per-route micro-sparkline series computed at ingest that captures token-cost and latency percentiles across a short window to make long-tail shifts visible in dashboards and alerts. 3) adaptive-alert-dampener: an alerting helper that automatically applies a temporary smoothing window and dynamic suppression for alerts that correlate with transient orbit spikes or cold-start waves. The description below is a single continuous narrative that contains the checklist, rollout plan, and rationale. Changes are backwards compatible: all new metrics are opt-in via a telemetry flag (ENV: RW_OBSERVABILITY_ORBIT=1). Checklist: - [x] Instrument runtime with orbit id and phase tagging (runtime, handler) - [x] Compute priority-sparkline at ingest (metrics pipeline) - [x] Add console dashboard panels and a compact sparkline component - [x] Implement adaptive-alert-dampener with conservative defaults (10m ramp) - [x] Add unit and integration tests + local replaybench for synthetic waves - [x] Documentation and migration notes included Related linear tickets: ENG-2145, ENG-2204. This PR is intended as a low-risk rollout: enable for 10% of traffic via rollout policy for 48h, evaluate alert reduction and false-suppression rate, then promote to 100% if alert dampening reduces churn without masking regressions. Backwards compatibility: clients and existing dashboards are unaffected unless the telemetry flag is enabled. The PR also documents a short guide (docs/observability/orbit.md) for SREs on how to interpret the orbit id and tune dampener thresholds. CI: initial run failed on lint (console jsonnet formatting) and a flaky replaybench test; fixes were pushed and CI passed on rerun. Merge: squash-merged after reviewers signoff and a short canary window on staging.

release_notes: Adds observability-orbit (invocation provenance id), priority-sparkline micro-series for per-tenant long-tail visibility, and an adaptive-alert-dampener to reduce alert churn from transient token spikes. Opt-in via RW_OBSERVABILITY_ORBIT. See docs/observability/orbit.md for rollout guidance.
review_comments: Ravi Singh: Can we guarantee orbit ids are stable across retries? If not, include a retry id join in the ingest to avoid double-counting.
Maya Gonzalez: Orbit id is stable per invocation origin; added a retry_id field and test in replaybench to prove de-dupe logic.
Hannah Li: Concerned about cardinality growth for tenant tags. Recommend downsampling high-cardinality labels and adding a sampling flag.
Maya Gonzalez: Implemented a tenant-sample path (configurable threshold) and documented the tradeoff in the runbook.
Josef Müller: Lint fail on dashboard jsonnet — small formatting suggestions applied and CI rerun.
Hannah Li: Approving after canary results look good and no alert suppression observed for our critical SLOs.
notes_on_rollout: Canary rollout via routing flags: 10% traffic for 48h against staging -> evaluate alert delta and false-suppression metric (alerts_suppressed_by_dampener/alerts_total). If rate < 1% and SLOs unaffected, promote to 100%.
observability_impact_summary: Expected: reduce noisy alert incidents by 30-60% for token-wave style bursts in first 48h. Cost: small CPU overhead in metrics-ingest to compute micro-sparklines; measured ~2% CPU increase in ingest workers at 10% traffic. Disabled by default.
notes: Follow-ups planned: 1) a lightweight viz in the SLO page that highlights orbits that contributed >50% of recent token-cost; 2) a CLI tool to query orbit provenance across traces.
